title: Understanding Drainage Venting Principles
description: A properly functioning drainage system relies just as heavily on air as it does on water. Drainage stacks require adequate venting to introduce air behind moving wastewater, preventing siphon action that can pull water traps dry and allow sewer gases to enter a building. When fixtures gurgle or drain slowly despite a clear pipe interior, the issue often points to a restricted or improperly sized vent stack rather than a simple downstream clog. Recognizing the relationship between drainage flow and atmospheric pressure is essential for diagnosing recurring drainage complaints.
